derived_results.claim: For the current discrete-time Gaussian step-change model, split misalignment has only g+1 observationally distinct offsets rather than a real-valued continuum.
derived_results.statement: With regular candidate spacing g=32, a changepoint between sampled observations induces one of x in {0,...,32}. A real-valued physical time between two samples yields the same observed P/Q partition as one integer x; only within-sample mixture changes would require a continuous offset model, and those are outside the present scope.
derived_results.consequence: The r72 continuum gap decomposes into 33 exact offsets times a one-dimensional Gaussian-alternative continuum along the KL level.

derived_results.claim: A pointwise exact-binomial upper bound on pair-failure probability can be transported to a continuum neighborhood using path-law KL and data processing through the pair-failure indicator.
derived_results.statement: At anchor a and offset x, let p_a=P_a(F) for the event F that both adjacent candidates fail their own weighted crossing thresholds, and let p_a<=u from one-sided Clopper-Pearson bounds on the two marginal failures. For target r, the joint path through the later adjacent candidate differs only in N_Q=H+g-x=128-x post-change observations, so D(path_r||path_a)=(128-x)D_KL(Q_r||Q_a). Data processing gives kl(p_r||p_a)<=D(path_r||path_a). If p_a<=u<p_r, monotonicity of binary KL gives kl(p_r||u)<=D(path_r||path_a). Therefore any r satisfying (128-x)D_KL(Q_r||Q_a)<=kl(beta_transport||u) is certified to have p_r<=beta_transport.
derived_results.gaussian_level: For P=N(0,1), exact I=0.5, parameterize Q_r=N(mu(r),r), mu(r)=sqrt(1+log r-r+1)=sqrt(2I+log r-r+1). Between two such alternatives, D_KL(Q_r||Q_a)=0.5[log(a/r)+(r+(mu(r)-mu(a))^2)/a-1].

derived_results.claim: The current I=0.5 scale {T=500,g=32,H=96,b=16} now has a randomized continuum certificate over the complete exact Gaussian KL=0.5 level and all 33 discrete offsets, rather than only a finite parameter grid.
derived_results.coverage: For every integer x in 0..32, KL-transport intervals from the 137 anchors covered the full exact-level variance-ratio interval in the double-precision root/merge calculation.
derived_results.scope: Randomized certificate on the exact level D_KL(Q||P)=0.5. It is not yet a theorem for all D_KL>=0.5. Coverage roots use ordinary float64 arithmetic, not machine-verified intervals. Negative mean shifts are covered by global sign symmetry.

derived_results.claim: If total individualized state is reduced from 10 to 9, the plausible route is to shrink the strong I=1 scale from four states to three via later deterministic activation, not to shrink the I=0.5 scale from three states to two.
derived_results.details: For I=1 with g=16,H=48, coarse exact-simulator scans improved from roughly 0.124 worst empirical pair failure at T=256 to about 0.081 at T~700 (3000 paths, 41 KL-level r points, all 17 offsets), with later tested T values remaining around 0.08-0.09. This is near the beta boundary and is not certified. For I=0.5 with H=64,g=32 (two states), later activation alone still left worst empirical pair failure around 0.21-0.27 in the tested scans, so that reduction is rejected as a current lead.

candidates_new.mechanism: Combine exact binomial upper bounds at adaptively chosen parameter anchors with KL data processing through the binary failure event to cover a continuous alternative family without assuming monotonicity of the detector statistic.
candidates_new.confidence: high for the information-theoretic transport lemma; medium-high for the current randomized I=0.5 certificate, limited by ordinary floating-point interval coverage and lack of raw-array durable serialization.

candidates_new.mechanism: Test I=1 with g=16,H=48 and delayed T0 around 700 or later, preserving only three individualized states on that scale while leaving I=0.5 and I=0.25 unchanged.
candidates_new.confidence: medium-low; engineering evidence only and close to beta=0.10.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The r72 finite 15x17 grid itself certifies the Gaussian parameter continuum.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected. Clopper-Pearson controls only Monte Carlo uncertainty at sampled parameter points. r73 adds a separate KL-transport cover to bridge between anchors.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Changepoint offset x must be treated as a continuous variable in the current model.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected for discrete-time step changes. Only the integer data partition matters; within-sample mixture changes are a different model.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The new I=0.5 certificate covers every Gaussian alternative with D_KL(Q||P)>=0.5.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not established. The present transport cover is only over the exact KL=0.5 level. Radial extension to larger KL remains open and must not be inferred.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The middle I=0.5 scale can likely be reduced from three individualized states to two by using H=64 and delaying activation.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Rejected as a current lead by engineering scans with worst empirical pair failure around 0.21-0.27, well above beta=0.10.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: The r73 Monte Carlo raw arrays are durably independently auditable from repository state alone.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not yet. The compact certificate stores seeds, procedure, aggregate worst counts, and SHA-256 hashes of in-memory arrays, but not the full raw arrays. A malformed oversized serialization attempt was repaired in the same path and the repaired compact summary is authoritative. Reproduction from seeds/procedure is required for raw-array audit.

frontier: Apply the same Clopper-Pearson plus binary-KL transport construction to the I=1 exact KL level, first testing the 3-state H=48 delayed-activation lead around T0~700. If it cannot obtain a nontrivial continuum margin, certify the current H=64/T0=256 scale instead.
Apply the same construction to the I=0.25 exact KL level with the current {T0=1024,g=64,H=192} design so all three scales have level-continuum evidence under one method.

Replace ordinary double-precision interval-root/coverage calculations by interval arithmetic or another auditable conservative numerical enclosure before calling the continuum cover machine-verified/adoption-grade.

Compare the separable candidate-wise null-infimum detector with the shared-null infimum-after-sum objective under the same small-state schedule after the three scale certificates are aligned.

exact_next_action: Run the r73 Clopper-Pearson + binary-KL transport certification on the I=1 exact Gaussian KL level. Start with the 9-state candidate T0 approximately 700, g=16, H=48, b=16, all integer offsets x=0..16. Adaptively add variance-ratio anchors until either a beta_transport<=0.09 continuum cover is obtained with explicit simultaneous Monte Carlo confidence or the required anchors/failure uppers show the H=48 design is too close to beta. If it fails, certify the existing I=1 H=64 scale. Then repeat for I=0.25/H=192 and only afterward attack the radial extension from exact KL levels to the full floors {D_KL>=I_floor}. Before adoption-grade use, rerun coverage roots with conservative interval arithmetic.
